source: Christoffersen, Hunter, Vicente (1996) A longitudinal study of the effects of ecological interface design on skill acquisition (Human Factors)
finding: Six-month daily DURESS II study. Physical-only (P) interface versus physical-plus-functional (P+F, EID-based). The gain was in consistency, not in the average.
numbers: Six months of quasi-daily practice. P group sometimes took up to 2 times longer on tasks, even after 5.5 months. Very little difference in average performance. N and F values not in the abstract (full text not obtained).
quote: P interface led to significantly less-consistent performance than did the P+F interface
limits: Abstract only; full text blocked (403). Tasks were start-up, tuning, shutdown and fault management on one microworld.
agent_relevance: The founding long-term result is 'fewer bad outliers', not 'better on average'. For S0, expect a gate to cut worst cases more than the mean.

source: Christoffersen, Hunter, Vicente (1995) Ecological Interface Design and Fault Management Performance: Long-Term Effects (HFES proceedings, six-month DURESS II study)
finding: Same six-month design, fault-focused report. EID interface gave faster fault detection, more accurate diagnosis and faster compensation, with large individual differences. At the end the groups swapped interfaces.
numbers: Six months; routine and non-routine faults. No N or effect sizes in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only via Crossref. Conference version; the journal paper (d01) stresses consistency over mean.
agent_relevance: Gives the direction of the novel-fault result (K17) but not its size. Still no numbers for a gate decision.

source: Vicente, Christoffersen, Pereklita (1995) Supporting operator problem solving through ecological interface design (IEEE SMC)
finding: Two experiments, P versus P+F interface on a thermal-hydraulic simulator. Exp 1 gave initial support to the abstraction-hierarchy display. Exp 2: good diagnosers began search at a high abstraction level and moved down, as predicted.
numbers: Two experiments; counts not in abstract. Prior experience with DURESS was the most reliable predictor of performance. Some evidence that theoretical expertise is needed for the full benefit.
limits: Abstract only (OpenAlex). Expertise moderates the effect; the weaker the user, the smaller the gain.
agent_relevance: Direct human analogue of top-down S0 search: effective solvers go purpose-first. Supports ordering, not a measured gain from prompting it.

source: Pawlak and Vicente (1996) Inducing effective operator control through ecological interface design (Int J Human-Computer Studies 44:653-688)
finding: Four weeks of daily practice with one of two interfaces, then normal events and unfamiliar faults. A later citation says studies of this kind generally favoured EID for novel scenarios. A deficiency of the P+F interface was also found: it lacked history information next to the emergent-feature displays.
numbers: Four weeks daily practice; 151 citations per Semantic Scholar. N, means and p values NOT obtained (publisher text closed; core.ac.uk PDF blocked).
limits: Seen only through search snippets and a machine summary, so opened=false. Do not quote numbers from this line.
agent_relevance: Even the founding paper reports a weakness: the abstract view needs history or trend information. An S0 model of purposes and functions may need a time dimension.

source: Maddox (1996) Critique of 'A Longitudinal Study of the Effects of Ecological Interface Design on Skill Acquisition' (Human Factors critique and response)
finding: A published critique exists. Its machine summary says the critic doubts the study tests the factor it claims to test. A response by the authors was printed with it.
numbers: 15 citations per Semantic Scholar. No numbers.
limits: Summary only; the critique text was not read.
agent_relevance: Shows the founding result was disputed in print. No independent replication found in this search.

source: Christoffersen, Hunter, Vicente (1998) A longitudinal study of the effects of ecological interface design on deep knowledge (IJHCS)
finding: Machine summary: EID can lead to a functionally organised knowledge base and better performance, but only if users actively reflect on the feedback the interface gives.
numbers: 55 citations per Semantic Scholar. No sample or effect numbers obtained.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: the benefit needs active reflection. Maps to our verify and reflect states; a passive display of the model may do little.

source: McIlroy and Stanton (2015) Ecological Interface Design Two Decades On: Whatever Happened to the SRK Taxonomy? (IEEE THMS)
finding: A comprehensive review of EID applications since Vicente and Rasmussen 1992. It reports how the method was used and reported, not a pooled effect on performance. 40% of reviewed applications do not cite the SRK taxonomy even though EID rests on it.
numbers: 40% of applications omit SRK. 79 citations per OpenAlex. No pooled effect size, no N of studies in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only. It is an application review, so it does not close the effect-size question. No other pooled EID estimate was found.
agent_relevance: Practitioners drop parts of the method and still call it EID. Any agent test must say exactly which parts of the hierarchy are in the prompt.

source: Reising and Sanderson (1998) Designing displays under ecological interface design: towards operationalizing semantic mapping; and (2002) Pasteurizer II
finding: Moving from work-domain equations to display shape needed 'open-ended artistry'. The authors offer three systematic routes (borrow theory depictions, adapt existing displays, invent forms from the state equations). The 2002 paper gives a process and a brief evaluation with subjective reports.
numbers: No inter-analyst agreement figures. 2002 evaluation described briefly, no statistics in abstract.
limits: Abstracts only. Addresses mapping to displays, not assignment of facts to levels.
agent_relevance: Supports K14: the method leaves analyst judgement open. For agents, run several samples and measure agreement.

source: Levy, Jacoby, Goldberg (2024) Same Task, More Tokens: the Impact of Input Length on the Reasoning Performance of LLMs (ACL 2024)
finding: FlenQA holds the task fixed and pads the input with irrelevant or duplicated text. Reasoning accuracy falls as input grows, well below the context limit. Chain of thought does not fix it.
numbers: Mean accuracy over tested models fell from 0.92 to 0.68 at 3000 tokens. Degradation visible beyond about 500 tokens. Two padding types (books and duplicated text) both hurt, books more. CoT helped on GPT-4, Mixtral, Mistral Medium, GPT-3.5 but lowered Gemini-Pro at longer lengths. Next-word accuracy correlates negatively with reasoning accuracy.
limits: Synthetic true/false reasoning tasks; padding is irrelevant text, not relevant guidance. Length cost is not shown for helpful scaffold text.
agent_relevance: Extra S0 text has a cost. A scaffold must be compared with a length-matched generic control; Wang 2024 and Kopka 2026 had none (gap 3 stays open for scaffolds).

source: Pfau, Merrill, Bowman (2024) Let's Think Dot by Dot: Hidden Computation in Transformer Language Models
finding: Meaningless filler tokens can match chain of thought on special algorithmic tasks in small transformers trained for it. Commercial LLMs do not benefit from filler tokens on the tasks tried.
numbers: Learning to use filler is hard and needs specific dense supervision (per paper). Accuracy tables not extracted this session.
limits: Small trained models on synthetic tasks; not a test of advice content versus length in prompts. Only the abstract and intro were read closely.
agent_relevance: Pure extra length gives no gain for deployed LLMs, so a gain from a scaffold is not just extra compute. Weak support for a content effect.

source: Cemri et al. (2025) Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST, 1,642 annotated traces)
finding: Failure taxonomy from 1,642 traces over 7 frameworks. Failures split into system design 41.8%, inter-agent misalignment 36.9%, task verification 21.3%. No category is keyed to misreading the problem class; the closest are disobeying the task specification (FM-1.1, 11.8%) and proceeding with wrong assumptions instead of asking (FM-2.2, 6.8%).
numbers: 14 failure modes. Human annotator kappa 0.88 on the final round (taxonomy built from 150 traces). LLM annotator accuracy 94%, kappa 0.77. Task failure rates 41% to 86.7% across the 7 systems. FM-3.1 premature end 6.2%, FM-3.2 missing verification 8.2%, FM-3.3 wrong verification 9.1%, FM-2.6 reasoning-action mismatch 13.2%.
limits: Multi-agent software, math and general-agent tasks; percentages are shares of failure modes observed, not rates per task. Not a work-domain-level taxonomy.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 partly answered: failures are mostly spec, coordination and verification, not raw ability. A gate that fixes the spec could address up to 41.8% of failures, and S6 verification 21.3%. Human annotators agreed well (kappa 0.88), a model for the inter-rater test we lack for WDA.

source: Cemri et al. (2025) MAST intervention study (same paper, appendix H and section 5)
finding: Improving only the agent role specification raised ChatDev task success by 9.4% with the same prompt and GPT-4o. Adding structural changes (topology and orchestration) gave +15.6% on ProgramDev.
numbers: +9.4% (role spec only), +15.6% (structural). Text says the gain is not on the base model.
limits: Single system (ChatDev) and one task set; no repeat across seeds reported in the text read.
agent_relevance: A clearer statement of purpose and roles, which is S0 content, moves success by about 9 points in one system. Supports testing the gate; not a WDA result.

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction in LLMs (Step-Back prompting)
finding: Ask the model first for the high-level concept or principle behind a question, then reason. This is the closest tested relative of an abstraction-level S0. Gains on STEM, knowledge QA and multi-hop tasks; most remaining errors are in the later reasoning, not the abstraction step.
numbers: PaLM-2L: MMLU physics +7%, chemistry +11%, TimeQA +27%, MuSiQue +7%. On MMLU physics it corrected 20.5% of baseline errors and introduced 11.9%. Over 90% of its residual errors are in the reasoning step; principle (abstraction) errors are a small share. Few exemplars suffice to teach abstraction.
limits: Single abstraction level (principles), not a five-level means-ends hierarchy. No length-matched control. Uses PaLM-2L, GPT-4 and Llama2-70B; gains smaller on GPT-4 than PaLM-2L.
agent_relevance: Evidence that going up one level before solving helps, and that abstraction errors are rare. It does not test purpose-to-form chains or why/how links. Gap 1 stays open.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Self-Discover: LLMs Self-Compose Reasoning Structures
finding: The model selects and composes reasoning modules into a task-specific structure before solving. This is the nearest test of a self-generated analysis against a given recipe (gap 3 and part of gap 1). Gains over CoT; 10-40 times fewer inference calls than self-consistency.
numbers: PaLM 2-L: BBH 67% vs CoT 60%, T4D 69% vs 40%, MATH 50.5% vs 42%. GPT-4: BBH 81% vs 75%, T4D 85% vs 52%, MATH 73% vs 71%. Self-composed structures were correct 87.5% of the time; 74.7% of MATH failures came from computation errors, not structure.
limits: Compared against CoT and Plan-and-Solve, not against a length-matched generic advice prompt. MATH gain is small (1 to 3 points on GPT-4). Seed modules are a fixed list written by humans.
agent_relevance: Self-chosen structure works without a human work analysis, and structure errors are the smaller part. Supports a self-generated S0 but only when seeded with a list of modules.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) CLAMBER: A Benchmark of Identifying and Clarifying Ambiguous Information Needs in LLMs
finding: About 12K items with a taxonomy of ambiguity; 3,600-item test sample. LLMs cannot reliably tell ambiguous from clear queries and CoT or few-shot add little, sometimes more overconfidence. Relevant to any label the model gives to a problem class.
numbers: Llama2-70B zero-shot accuracy 50.37, F1 34.27. ChatGPT accuracy 54.25%, F1 52.77%. Models label most queries ambiguous. Few-shot raised expected calibration error for Vicuna-13B by 4.19 points. For ChatGPT self-contradiction cases, 81.97% of errors were false negatives.
limits: 2023-era models (Vicuna, Llama2, ChatGPT); newer models likely better but not measured here. Single-turn queries, not agent work.
agent_relevance: Near-chance class labelling means a self-assigned S0 class can be wrong often. Gap 4 partly answered: label accuracy should be measured and a wrong label needs a cheap exit. Also bears on gap 10 (ask-or-act).

source: Becker et al. (2025) Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity (METR randomized trial)
finding: Randomised trial in real repositories. Developers expected AI to speed them up, but tasks took longer with AI. Benchmarks and expert forecasts pointed the other way.
numbers: 16 developers, 246 tasks (about 2.0 hours each). Forecast speed-up before: 24%. Estimate after: 20% speed-up. Measured: 19% MORE time with AI. Economists forecast 39% shorter, ML experts 38%.
limits: 16 developers, early-2025 tools, mature repos they knew well; authors list setting-specific factors. Not a scaffold test.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 counterpart: benchmark and expert expectation overstated live results by a wide margin. Treat any S0 gain on a benchmark as an upper bound and keep a live-task holdout.

source: Gap 8 search: Chang Lee and Rondinelli 2026 decision-ladder agent
finding: Search of the web and OpenAlex found no paper matching Chang Lee, Rondinelli, decision ladder, cognitive work analysis. Nearby quantum chemistry agent papers (El Agente Q, Graphico, Quntur) did not mention the decision ladder in the snippets.
numbers: No numbers found; 24.9% to 44.1% coverage figures remain unverified.
limits: Negative result under rate limits (OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar returned 429 repeatedly). Not evidence the paper does not exist.
agent_relevance: Keep K06 flagged unverified; do not rely on the figures.

source: Gap 5 search: inter-rater agreement for abstraction-hierarchy analysis
finding: A Crossref query found no study that reports agreement between analysts on which facts go on which hierarchy level. The only title near the topic is a chapter 'Work Domain Analysis Using the Abstraction Hierarchy: Two Contrasting Cases', no abstract available.
numbers: No kappa or percent agreement found for human WDA. For comparison MAST reports kappa 0.88 for human failure-mode labels.
limits: Absence under limited search (one engine). Chapter title suggests different models of one domain, not confirmed.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 stays open for humans. For agents it is cheap to test: sample the analysis several times and score level-assignment overlap.
